newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar supplies.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar supplies.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Wednesday after heavier-than-usual dollar positions propelled dollar sales, dealers said.
They said fund inflows on depositary receipts issues by Housing and Commercial Bank also added to selling pressure on the dollar.
The won closed at 893.60, compared with Tuesday's closing of 894.40, which is today's opening level. It moved between 893.20 and 894.40.
"Trading was slow today. But supplies of dollars slightly outweighed demand," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said fears of the central bank's dollar sales intervention at above 894.40 also promted dollar unwinding.
But they said the dollar's fall was limited by fears that troubles at the Kia Group would lead to depreciation of the won.
"Dollar buying will revive again on Thursday because of much fewer dollar supplies tomorrow," said a foreign bank dealer.
Trading was forecast to range from 893.00 to 895.00 on Thursday. --KIM MYONG-HWAN (822) 727 5645
